notes:
Summary: Quicksilver RT is building a live pricing & personalization layer for retail trading desks. Extremely latency-sensitive (p95 < 25ms for rerank/score path) and cost-conscious at scale. Wants clear knobs to trade latency vs. per-token cost. Team initially evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Optimize recommendations.

Stakeholders: CTO (Anika Rao) - cares about predictable throughput; Head of ML (Samir Patel) - wants quantization guidance and dev ergonomics; Platform lead (Ruth Kim) - VPC, peering, and audit logging are deal breakers.

Technical asks from discovery call:
- Baseline perf for 7B and 13B variants using 512-token context for reranking micro-benchmarks.
- Examples of batching configs that keep p95 < 25ms at 250 qps.
- KV/prefix caching behavior for multi-step chat where many calls re-use same context.
- Quantization impact matrix: latency vs. generation quality for int8/int4 and recommended fallback policies.
- Cost modeling: per-route cost at 100k qps equivalent across hosted vs dedicated.

Quotes & color: "If we can't show sub-25ms p95 in a realistic perf test, we can't move forward this quarter." — Samir Patel.

Security & procurement: Provided SOC2 and ISO questions; security team asked for KMS integration diagram and audit log retention SLA. Legal requested DPA for EU residency clause.

POC scope agreed: 7-day perf run, two model sizes (7B and 13B quantized), traffic replay of production traces (sampled), cost report, and a short handoff doc for SRE. Diego to provide perf harness template; Quicksilver to supply anonymized trace and a network topology doc for VPC peering.

Internal notes (AE): Keep messaging tight on batching tips: prefer continuous batching with max-latency 8ms cap; suggest adaptive batching + prefix caching for chat flows; show real numbers for token-level cost reduction from 16-bit -> int8 -> int4 conversions.

Sales cadence: Weekly check-ins, technical syncs Tue 11am PST. Execs want a demo to board in first two weeks of April.
